title: ¿Cómo es?
goal: Describe things and people: size, age, colour and character, with ser.

lessons.title: Big and small
lessons.notes:
Adjectives usually come **after** the noun: **un libro nuevo** (a new book), **una casa grande** - the reverse of English.
They match the noun in gender and number, like nationalities did:
**-o** words have four forms: nuevo, nueva, nuevos, nuevas.
**-e** and most consonant endings have two: grande, grandes.
**El libro es pequeño. La mesa es pequeña. Los libros son pequeños.**
A few common ones can go first and then lose the -o: **un buen día**, **un mal día**. **Muy** (very) goes before: **muy bonito**.

items.note: Before a masculine noun: buen (un buen libro).
Before a masculine noun: mal (un mal día).

sentences.es: Carlos no es alto, es bajo.
accept_en: Carlos is not tall, he is short.
It is a very good computer.
It is a very big problem.

sentences.es: El perro es pequeño y el gato es viejo.
sentences.en: The dog is small and the cat is old.

lessons.title: Colours
lessons.notes:
Colours are adjectives, so they go after the noun and match it: **un carro rojo**, **una mochila roja**, **dos mochilas rojas**.
Colours ending in -e or a consonant only add -s / -es: **verde → verdes**, **azul → azules**, **gris → grises**.
**Naranja** and **rosa** are also the names of things (an orange, a rose), so many people don't change them at all: **unas mochilas naranja**.
Ask **¿De qué color es?** - literally 'of what colour is it?'. Brown is **marrón** in many places, **café** in Mexico and Central America.

sentences.es: Los lápices son rojos y azules.
sentences.en: The pencils are red and blue.

sentences.es: Mi color favorito es el naranja.

lessons.title: What are people like?
lessons.notes:
**¿Cómo es Ana?** asks what Ana is like - her looks or her character. Answer with **ser**, because it's about who she is: **Es simpática.**
**Simpático** is a false friend: it means nice, friendly, easy to like - not 'sympathetic'.
Words ending in -e or a consonant don't change for a woman: **Ana es inteligente**, **Carlos es joven**. In the plural, **joven → jóvenes** (an accent keeps the stress where it was).
For older people **mayor** is kinder than viejo. Link two ideas with **y** (and) or **pero** (but): **Es serio pero simpático.**

items.en: what is he / she / it like?

items.note: Always feminine, even for a man.

sentences.es: Ana es simpática y muy inteligente.
sentences.en: Ana is nice and very intelligent.
accept_en: Ana is friendly and very smart.
Ana is nice and very smart.

sentences.es: La señora es mayor pero muy divertida.
sentences.en: The lady is older but very funny.
accept_en: The woman is elderly but very fun.
The lady is old but a lot of fun.
He is a very good person.
She is a very good person.

sentences.es: El hombre es alto y guapo.
sentences.en: The man is tall and handsome.
accept_en: The man is tall and good-looking.

sentences.es: Mi amiga es guapa y simpática.
sentences.en: My friend is pretty and nice.
accept_en: My friend is beautiful and friendly.
My friend is good-looking and nice.

lessons.title: Describing places and things
lessons.notes:
Use **ser** to say what something is like - its lasting qualities: **La casa es grande. El hotel es caro.**
A question can simply flip the order: **¿Es caro el hotel?** (is the hotel expensive?) - or just raise your voice: **¿El hotel es caro?**
Latin America says **el carro** (or el auto); Spain says **el coche**.
The name of a language is masculine and has no capital: **el español**, **el inglés**. 'Spanish is easy' = **El español es fácil.**

items.note: Spain: el coche. Argentina, Chile: el auto.

sentences.es: La casa es grande y bonita.
sentences.en: The house is big and pretty.
accept_en: The house is large and beautiful.
The house is big and nice.

sentences.es: El carro es nuevo pero barato.
sentences.en: The car is new but cheap.
accept_en: The car is new but inexpensive.

sentences.es: Australia es un país muy grande.
sentences.en: Australia is a very big country.
accept_en: Australia is a very large country.

sentences.es: Es un carro rojo muy caro.
sentences.en: It's a very expensive red car.
accept_en: It is a very expensive red car.

sentences.es: El español no es difícil, es divertido.
accept_en: Spanish is not difficult, it is fun.
